\begin{abstract}

accuracy over \rftnum{E05}{runs} runs.

\section{Introduction}

% Your text, and copies of snippets between % rft-begin and % rft-end lines: adapt a copy to the
% narrative as you like; when its snippet changes, the copy is flagged for review.

Mixing augmentations such as CutMix~\cite{R07} and mixup~\cite{zhang2018mixup} are standard; see
Definition~\ref{S01}, Lemma~\ref{S07} and Figure~\ref{S03}.

% rft-begin S01 2a248ff2
\begin{definition}[CutMix]\label{S01}
Given two labelled images $(x_A, y_A)$ and $(x_B, y_B)$, CutMix~\cite{R07} forms
$\tilde{x} = M \odot x_A + (1 - M) \odot x_B$ and $\tilde{y} = \lambda y_A + (1 - \lambda) y_B$,
where $M$ is a binary box mask and $\lambda$ is the fraction of $x_A$ that it keeps.
\end{definition}
% rft-end S01

\section{Method}

% rft-begin S04 df889d41
We train a ResNet-50 for 200 epochs with SGD, a cosine schedule and a batch size of 256. CutMix is
applied to every batch with $\lambda \sim \mathrm{Beta}(1, 1)$.
% rft-end S04

\section{Results}

% rft-begin S02 ac5a9b18
\paragraph{CutMix at 1k images.}
In our setting, CutMix reaches \rftnum{E05}{acc.1k}\% top-1 accuracy with 1k labelled images. % was: against the full set
% rft-end S02

% rft-begin S07 0badf00d
\begin{lemma}[Mixing bound]\label{S07}
The mixed label $\tilde{y}$ lies in the convex hull of $y_A$ and $y_B$.
\end{lemma}
